articles.title: Eric Dane Says ALS Symptoms Started Months Before Diagnosis. What He Shared About His Disease
articles.summary: Before actor Eric Dane died after a two-year battle with ALS in Feb. 2026, he shared details about life with ALS and how the illness progressed.
articles.body: Actor Eric Dane died on Feb. 19, 2026, at 53 years old, 10 months after revealing he’d been diagnosed with ALS. According to his death certificate obtained by NBC News, he died of respiratory failure. “With heavy hearts, we share that Eric Dane passed on Thursday afternoon following a courageous battle with ALS,” his family said in a statement to NBC News. “He spent his final days surrounded by dear friends, his devoted wife, and his two beautiful daughters, Billie and Georgia, who were the center of his world. Throughout his journey with ALS, Eric became a passionate advocate for awareness and research, determined to make a difference for others facing the same fight.” In interviews, on social media and through his advocacy work, Dane shared details about how the disease progressed, discussed his symptoms and revealed the challenges of living with ALS. Now, nine months after his death, Dane’s posthumous memoir, “My Book of Days: A Memoir in Moments,” publishing on Nov. 3, sheds even more light on his life before and during his ALS battle. Here's what to know. What Was Eric Dane’s Cause of Death? Dane died from respiratory failure, according to his death certificate. It notes ALS, a neurodegenerative disease that impacts muscle control, as the underlying cause of death. The actor, known for his roles in “Euphoria” and “Grey’s Anatomy,” first revealed he had the disease in an April 2025 interview with People. “I am grateful to have my loving family by my side as we navigate this next chapter,” Dane told the outlet. He also said he planned to continue acting. When Did Eric Dane’s ALS Symptoms Start? In a June 2025 interview, Dane shared that his ALS symptoms had started about a year and a half prior — late 2023 or early 2024. “I started experiencing some weakness in my right hand,” he said in the interview with ABC News. At first, he blamed overzealous texting, but when the weakness progressed, he consulted a hand specialist, who then referred him to another specialist. “I went and saw a neurologist, and the neurologist sent me to another neurologist and said that ‘this is way above my pay grade.’” In an interview with The Cut in December 2025, Dane’s wife, Rebecca Gayheart, recalled his sudden difficulties using chopsticks and dropping his food. “He was initially diagnosed with a few other things, but he had this sinking feeling that it was something more serious,” she said. After nine months of searching for answers, he was diagnosed with ALS. By June 2025, he only had one functioning arm. “My left side is functioning, my right side has completely stopped working,” he told ABC News. He knew things would change soon. He could feel the strength in his left arm deteriorating. “It’s going,” he said, “I feel, like, maybe in a couple — a few more months, I won’t have my left either.” “It’s sobering,” he added. In a September 2025 video shared on social media, Dane’s speech had changed, his words slow and slurred. In it, he stressed the importance of finding a cure for ALS. Dane eventually lost his ability to speak, but used an AI voice to communicate. “It really made him hopeful. ... He was really emotional about it — we all were, and it was just such a gift,” Gayheart said. Gayheart also revealed to The Cut that Dane was being cared for by nurses 24/7. How Long Did Eric Dane Have ALS? Dane was diagnosed with ALS in 2024, after noticing weakness in his right hand. He lived with it for two years. Since learning he had the disease, Dane said he’d never forget those three letters: ALS. “It’s on me the second I wake up,” he told ABC News. Still, he kept on, sharing positive updates. “I feel great when I’m at work,” he told E! News in June 2025. “Of course, there have been some sort of setbacks, but I feel pretty good. My spirit is always pretty buoyant, so at the end of the day, that’s all that matters.” In unreleased footage Dane filmed with I AM ALS, an advocacy organization, he said life with this diagnosis is "uncharted territory." "I'm learning as I go. I'm just trying to, like, walk through this thing with as much grace and dignity as I can so I can show my kids: this is how you do this." Having ALS is hard, he added, but it's tough for his loved ones too. In his final interview, Dane shared four messages for his daughters. "Live in the present.""Fall in love.""Find your people.""Fight with every ounce of your being." Since Dane’s passing, Gayheart shared updates about how she and their daughters are coping. “You know, we’re hanging in there,” Gayheart told People in Sept. 2026. “I think it’s definitely a challenging season, but we’re doing our best.” “The girls are both in high school — which is also a big transition under any circumstance — so I’m just staying close to my kids,” she added. Dane was unsure about writing a memoir at first, Gayheart told People. But she’s “grateful he did, because it gives my girls the opportunity to know their dad as a human being,” she said about their children. What Is ALS? ALS, short for amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, also known as Lou Gehrig’s disease, is a degenerative neurological disease that impacts nerve function. The illness targets nerve cells in the spine and brain, according to the Cleveland Clinic, causing progressive deterioration of muscle control. There is no way to prevent it, and there is no cure. As the disease evolves, people with ALS can experience muscle weakness, cramps, stiffness, drooling, fatigue, trouble swallowing and trouble speaking, the Cleveland Clinic adds. Eventually, patients might lose their ability to walk, stand, breathe and speak. Eventually, symptoms can lead to respiratory failure, the Cleveland Clinic says. Respiratory failure is life-threatening because it keeps people from being able to breathe in enough oxygen. Other complications of ALS include feelings of overwhelm, stress, depression and anxiety. What Causes ALS? Researchers are still investigating what causes ALS, but scientists believe that, for some, it's genetic and, for others, it's caused by environmental factors, such as exposure to toxins, according to the Cleveland Clinic. Some people can inherit the genetic makeup that causes ALS, but it's more common that someone's ALS is sporadic. What is the ALS Life Expectancy? Though there are treatment options that can help slow its progression, ALS will shorten life expectancy. After diagnosis, patients are expected to live between three and five more years, according to the Cleveland Clinic. "An estimated 30% of people live five years or more, and 10% to 20% live at least 10 years," it adds. Dane died two years after receiving his diagnosis. What Are the Treatments for ALS? ALS is irreversible; however, there are ways to slow the progression of symptoms, according to the Cleveland Clinic. These treatments include: MedicationTherapy or rehabilitationNutrition protocols to support the additional energy expenditure ALS causes, and support healthy bones and weightBreathing support

articles.title: Unimed Teresina implanta pulseira para acompanhar cirurgias em tempo real | G1
articles.standfirst: Hospital Unimed Teresina é pioneiro no Piauí com tecnologia que melhora a comunicação com acompanhantes e oferece mais tranquilidade durante a espera.
articles.summary: Hospital Unimed Teresina é pioneiro no Piauí com tecnologia que melhora a comunicação com acompanhantes e oferece mais tranquilidade durante a espera.
articles.body:
A tecnologia permite aos acompanhantes acompanhar, em tempo real, as diferentes etapas da jornada cirúrgica. — Foto: Unimed Teresina

A espera por notícias de um familiar durante uma cirurgia costuma ser marcada pela ansiedade e pela preocupação. Para tornar esse momento mais tranquilo, o Hospital Unimed Teresina implementou uma tecnologia que permite aos acompanhantes acompanhar, em tempo real, as diferentes etapas da jornada cirúrgica. Por meio de uma pulseira inteligente, familiares podem receber informações diretamente pelo celular, desde a preparação do paciente até sua recuperação após o procedimento.

O Hospital Unimed Teresina é a primeira instituição hospitalar do Piauí a implementar a tecnologia de acompanhamento individualizado da jornada cirúrgica. O funcionamento é simples. Ao dar entrada no Centro Cirúrgico, o paciente recebe uma pulseira inteligente equipada com tecnologia Bluetooth, que emite sinais captados por sensores instalados em diferentes ambientes do setor. Esses dados são enviados automaticamente à plataforma, permitindo identificar a etapa em que o paciente se encontra, como o pré-operatório, o início e o término da cirurgia, a recuperação pós-anestésica e a liberação para o leito.

Para acompanhar essas informações, o familiar precisa apenas escanear um QR Code disponibilizado na recepção do hospital, informar o código da cirurgia e a data de nascimento do paciente. Em seguida, basta selecionar a opção “Acompanhar cirurgia” para visualizar as atualizações pelo celular. A plataforma também permite compartilhar o acompanhamento por meio de um link enviado pelo WhatsApp, possibilitando que outros familiares, mesmo distantes, recebam informações sobre o andamento do atendimento.

Para o presidente da Unimed Teresina , Rodrigo Pereira, a implementação representa mais um passo na modernização dos serviços hospitalares, colocando a tecnologia a serviço das pessoas. “Investir em inovação é, acima de tudo, investir em uma assistência mais segura, eficiente e humanizada. Sabemos que uma cirurgia é um momento delicado não apenas para o paciente, mas também para toda a família. Com essa tecnologia, queremos oferecer mais tranquilidade, informação e acolhimento, ao mesmo tempo em que aprimoramos nossos processos internos. Nosso compromisso é fazer com que cada avanço tecnológico se transforme em mais qualidade no cuidado com as pessoas”, destaca.

Além de facilitar o acesso às informações, a plataforma representa uma importante ferramenta de apoio à gestão hospitalar. Isso porque o acompanhamento automatizado permite visualizar o percurso dos pacientes, identificar possíveis atrasos e avaliar o tempo necessário para a realização de cada etapa do atendimento.

Segundo o superintendente de Recursos Próprios da Unimed Teresina, Hugo Neves, a iniciativa foi desenvolvida para ampliar o controle dos processos assistenciais e proporcionar maior eficiência à rotina do hospital. “Implantamos essa tecnologia porque queremos acompanhar toda a jornada do paciente, desde sua entrada até a alta, identificando o tempo de espera, a recuperação e o deslocamento para o leito. Todas essas informações são analisadas para que possamos aprimorar continuamente o atendimento ao nosso beneficiário. Nosso objetivo é fortalecer a segurança assistencial, garantir o cumprimento dos protocolos e oferecer um cuidado cada vez mais qualificado”, explica.

De acordo com o gestor, as informações também são reunidas em painéis digitais de monitoramento, conhecidos como dashboards, que permitem acompanhar indicadores relacionados ao tempo de transporte dos pacientes, higienização das salas, duração dos procedimentos, anestesia e recuperação pós-operatória. Com esses dados, a equipe pode identificar necessidades de ajustes e tomar decisões com maior agilidade.

“Vamos trabalhar com indicadores e processos bem definidos, acompanhando os tempos de cada etapa e acionando as equipes sempre que necessário. Isso nos permite melhorar a eficiência operacional, otimizar recursos e, principalmente, garantir que o paciente receba a assistência adequada em cada momento da sua jornada”, acrescenta Hugo Neves.

Na avaliação do diretor clínico do Hospital Unimed Teresina, Jório Neiva, a tecnologia fortalece a segurança e a organização do atendimento, mas deve atuar sempre como complemento ao trabalho dos profissionais de saúde. “A tecnologia é uma aliada para tornar o percurso cirúrgico mais organizado e eficiente, desde a preparação até as diferentes etapas do atendimento. Nosso compromisso é utilizar a inovação para qualificar a assistência e tornar a experiência hospitalar mais acolhedora, sem perder de vista a humanização. Ela apoia o trabalho das equipes, mas não substitui o contato direto, a atenção dos profissionais e o diálogo com pacientes e familiares”, ressalta.

Mais informação e tranquilidade para as famílias

Na rotina do Centro Cirúrgico, a expectativa é que a ferramenta também contribua para reduzir a necessidade de deslocamentos e solicitações constantes de informações na recepção, permitindo que os profissionais concentrem ainda mais atenção no atendimento aos pacientes.

A gestora do Centro Cirúrgico, Alessandra Oliveira, explica que a possibilidade de compartilhar as atualizações com outros familiares é um dos principais diferenciais da solução, especialmente para quem acompanha um procedimento cirúrgico e precisa manter outras pessoas informadas.

“O acompanhante consegue visualizar as informações pelo celular e compartilhar o acesso com familiares por meio do WhatsApp, independentemente de onde estejam. Isso ajuda a reduzir a ansiedade provocada pela falta de notícias e evita que uma única pessoa precise ficar repassando informações durante todo o procedimento”, destaca.

Segundo Alessandra, a tecnologia também permite identificar os pacientes que já estão no hospital, organizar melhor a distribuição das equipes nos horários de maior movimento e planejar os procedimentos cirúrgicos de acordo com a disponibilidade da estrutura e dos profissionais.

“Com uma visão mais clara de toda a jornada, conseguimos melhorar a comunicação entre os setores, organizar a rotina e proporcionar mais agilidade aos processos. Ao mesmo tempo, a equipe pode manter sua concentração no cuidado direto ao paciente, enquanto os familiares recebem as atualizações pela plataforma”, explica.

Uma inovação que nasceu da experiência de uma paciente

A proposta de aproximar pacientes, familiares e equipes hospitalares surgiu de uma experiência pessoal da fundadora da Dr. Next, Juliana Barros. Em 2022, após receber o diagnóstico de câncer de mama, ela precisou passar por três procedimentos cirúrgicos em um intervalo de nove meses. Durante esse período, percebeu como a falta de informações sobre o andamento das cirurgias afetava emocionalmente sua família.

“Todas as vezes que eu entrava no Centro Cirúrgico, meu pai passava mal na sala de espera. Eu entrava mais aflita com a experiência da minha família e com a falta de comunicação com eles do que com o próprio procedimento. Foi a partir dessa vivência que surgiu a ideia de desenvolver uma solução que pudesse transformar essa experiência”, relata.

A partir dessa necessidade, a plataforma foi desenvolvida para conectar o acompanhamento da jornada cirúrgica à gestão hospitalar. Utilizando sensores, pulseiras inteligentes e recursos de inteligência artificial, o sistema permite visualizar o fluxo de pacientes e produzir informações que auxiliam no planejamento das atividades.

“Com os sinais emitidos pela pulseira e captados pelos sensores espalhados pelo Centro Cirúrgico, conseguimos identificar onde o paciente está, em qual momento da jornada ele se encontra e quanto tempo permanece em cada etapa. Essas informações permitem que as equipes tenham uma atuação mais ágil e preditiva, inclusive no planejamento da higienização das salas e do transporte dos pacientes”, finaliza Juliana.

articles.title: Torcedor baleado em Duque de Caxias está em estado grave no Rio | G1
articles.standfirst: Homem está em estado grave no Moacyr do Carmo após ser atingido em suposta briga de torcida.
articles.summary: Um torcedor baleado em Duque de Caxias está em estado grave após ser atacado por homens armados enquanto esperava amigos para ir ao jogo entre Vasco e Flamengo.
articles.body:
Fila no Hospital Moacyr do Carmo, em Caxias — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

Um homem foi baleado na manhã desta quinta-feira (29) na Avenida Governador Leonel de Moura Brizola enquanto estava parado em um ponto de ônibus no centro de Duque de Caxias, na Baixada Fluminense.

De acordo com informações policiais, amigos seguiam de táxi para o Maracanã, onde o Vasco e o Flamengo se enfrentam nesta noite. Eles fizeram uma parada na garagem da Jurema para esperar outro amigo que iria junto.

Um dos homens que estava no táxi relatou à polícia que eles ficaram parados por cerca de 5 minutos no local quando cerca de seis ou sete homens se aproximaram. Eles seriam de uma torcida organizada.

Ao se aproximarem do grupo, segundo a testemunha, eles fizeram disparos acreditando que eles pertenciam a um grupo de torcida organizada rival porque o taxista, que só estava realizando a viagem, estava com uma calça de time e um deles usava uma camisa preta.

Um dos torcedores foi atingido no pescoço e levado de táxi para o Hospital Municipal Moacyr do Carmo, onde ficou internado com quadro de saúde grave.

"Após avaliação médica, paciente foi encaminhado imediatamente ao centro cirúrgico, onde passou por procedimento. A direção informa que, no momento, paciente está em unidade pós operatória, em traqueostomia e seu quadro de saúde é grave", informou a prefeitura de Duque de Caxias.

O caso foi registrado na 59ª DP (Duque de Caxias) e é investigado como tentativa de homicídio.

articles.title: Acreditação ONA: Hospital Erasto Gaertner conquista Nível 1 em qualidade e segurança | G1
articles.standfirst: Reconhecimento resulta de avaliação externa dos padrões de qualidade e segurança e marca uma etapa no aprimoramento dos processos hospitalares.
articles.summary: Reconhecimento resulta de avaliação externa dos padrões de qualidade e segurança e marca uma etapa no aprimoramento dos processos hospitalares.
articles.body:
O Hospital Erasto Gaertner, referência em oncologia em Curitiba, recebeu a Acreditação ONA Nível 1, reconhecimento concedido após uma avaliação externa dos padrões de qualidade e segurança aplicáveis à instituição. O processo envolveu diferentes áreas do hospital e mobilizou equipes assistenciais e de apoio em uma jornada de revisão, organização e aprimoramento dos processos de trabalho.

A acreditação representa uma etapa importante na trajetória do Erasto Gaertner para fortalecer a qualidade e a segurança da assistência. A avaliação considera práticas e processos institucionais que fazem parte do cuidado realizado diariamente por profissionais de diferentes áreas.

Entre os aspectos relacionados à segurança do paciente estão a identificação correta, as conferências de informações, a comunicação entre equipes, os protocolos assistenciais e a gestão de riscos. Esses mecanismos funcionam como barreiras de segurança ao longo da jornada do paciente e contribuem para a organização dos processos de atendimento.

O Nível 1 da acreditação da Organização Nacional de Acreditação (ONA), denominado “Acreditado”, reconhece o atendimento aos requisitos estabelecidos para essa etapa. A conquista, porém, não encerra o trabalho: o acompanhamento dos processos, a identificação de oportunidades de melhoria e o desenvolvimento contínuo das equipes permanecem como parte da rotina institucional.

A Acreditação ONA é um processo de avaliação externa que verifica o atendimento a padrões de qualidade e segurança aplicáveis às instituições de saúde. O reconhecimento é organizado por níveis, de acordo com os requisitos estabelecidos para cada etapa.

No caso do Hospital Erasto Gaertner, a conquista do Nível 1 representa o reconhecimento do atendimento aos critérios correspondentes à etapa inicial da acreditação. A avaliação envolveu diferentes processos da instituição e exigiu a participação de profissionais de áreas assistenciais e de apoio.

O processo permite analisar práticas institucionais e identificar oportunidades de aprimoramento. A partir dessa avaliação, a instituição mantém o trabalho de acompanhamento e revisão de suas rotinas, com atenção aos procedimentos que contribuem para a qualidade e a segurança da assistência.

Segurança do paciente: práticas presentes no atendimento

A segurança do paciente depende de processos organizados e da atuação integrada das equipes ao longo do atendimento. Entre as práticas relacionadas a esse objetivo estão a identificação correta do paciente, a conferência de informações, a comunicação entre profissionais, o cumprimento de protocolos e o acompanhamento de riscos.

Essas ações podem ocorrer em diferentes momentos da jornada assistencial e nem sempre são percebidas diretamente pelos pacientes. Ainda assim, fazem parte do trabalho necessário para organizar o cuidado e reduzir a possibilidade de falhas nos processos.

A avaliação que resultou na Acreditação ONA Nível 1 considerou padrões aplicáveis à instituição e mobilizou profissionais de diferentes setores. A conquista dá visibilidade ao trabalho realizado pelas equipes para revisar e organizar práticas que contribuem para a qualidade e a segurança hospitalar.

Qualidade hospitalar é construída no dia a dia

A preparação para a avaliação externa envolveu profissionais de áreas assistenciais e de apoio, que participaram da organização e revisão de processos, documentos e práticas institucionais. O trabalho integrou diferentes setores em torno de objetivos comuns relacionados à qualidade e à segurança do paciente.

No cotidiano hospitalar, esse esforço se traduz em rotinas como a conferência de informações, a comunicação entre equipes, o cumprimento de protocolos e o acompanhamento de riscos. A consistência dessas práticas depende da participação dos profissionais e da revisão contínua dos processos de trabalho.

O reconhecimento também representa uma oportunidade de valorizar as equipes que contribuem para manter e aprimorar essas rotinas. A qualidade da assistência é resultado de um trabalho coletivo, desenvolvido em diferentes áreas e etapas do atendimento.

O que muda após a Acreditação ONA Nível 1?

A conquista da Acreditação ONA Nível 1 marca uma etapa na jornada de aprimoramento do Hospital Erasto Gaertner. O reconhecimento indica o atendimento aos requisitos estabelecidos para esse nível, mas o trabalho institucional continua após a avaliação.

Acompanhar processos, aprender com as experiências do cotidiano e identificar oportunidades de melhoria são atividades permanentes. A instituição segue trabalhando para desenvolver suas práticas e fortalecer a integração entre as equipes.

Nesse contexto, qualidade e segurança não ficam restritas ao período de avaliação externa. São construídas no dia a dia, por meio de procedimentos, comunicação entre profissionais e atenção às diferentes etapas do cuidado.

A importância da acreditação para instituições de saúde

Processos de acreditação permitem que instituições de saúde sejam avaliadas a partir de padrões definidos de qualidade e segurança. A avaliação externa contribui para examinar práticas e processos e reconhecer o atendimento aos requisitos correspondentes ao nível alcançado.

No Hospital Erasto Gaertner, a Acreditação ONA Nível 1 integra uma trajetória de organização e aprimoramento das rotinas institucionais. A participação de diferentes áreas também evidencia a importância do trabalho integrado entre equipes assistenciais e de apoio para sustentar os processos relacionados à assistência.

A continuidade desse trabalho depende do acompanhamento das práticas, da análise de oportunidades de melhoria e do envolvimento dos profissionais na rotina hospitalar.

O Hospital Erasto Gaertner é uma instituição filantrópica e referência em oncologia, integrada à Liga Paranaense de Combate ao Câncer. Com atendimento especializado em diferentes áreas relacionadas ao cuidado oncológico, recebe pacientes de diversas regiões e mantém atuação voltada à assistência, ao ensino, à pesquisa e à inovação.

Mais de 75% dos atendimentos são realizados pelo Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS), contribuindo para ampliar o acesso ao tratamento oncológico especializado.

articles.title: Israeli strikes hit Gaza as Health Ministry urges Rafah opening
articles.summary: Gaza’s Health Ministry says dozens died awaiting treatment abroad as Israeli attacks continue despite a ‘ceasefire’.
articles.body:
At least two people have been killed in the latest Israeli attacks on Gaza, as the Ministry of Health in the strip calls for the Rafah crossing to be opened to allow sick and wounded Palestinians to leave for treatment.

Israeli attacks across Gaza continue at a “very high pace” on Thursday, with drone strikes hitting the centre and north of the territory over the past few hours, according to Al Jazeera’s Ashraf Abu Amra.

Reporting from Deir el-Balah, Abu Amra said an Israeli drone fired two missiles in quick succession at a civilian car in the middle of the Maghazi refugee camp in central Gaza, killing two Palestinians and wounding others.

The wounded were taken to Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital, where they were rushed into operating theatres or admitted to intensive care. One is in critical condition.

“The strike was sudden and came without prior warning,” Abu Amra said, noting that Israeli aircraft are flying at low altitude across all areas of the strip.

Earlier, an Israeli strike in Jabalia, in northern Gaza, wounded a Palestinian who was taken to al-Shifa Hospital in Gaza City.

Abu Amra said attacks were escalating east of Jabalia in the Halawa camp, one of the largest displacement camps in the north, where Israeli forces stationed along the edges of the so-called “Yellow Line” have begun firing directly at tents sheltering displaced families.

In eastern Gaza City, explosions have been heard in the Shujayea, Tuffah and Zeitoun neighbourhoods as a result of Israeli artillery shelling. Israeli forces are also carrying out large-scale demolitions in areas under their control behind the “Yellow Line”, including east of Deir el-Balah, Khan Younis and Gaza City, and in Beit Lahiya in the north, destroying homes and what remains of local infrastructure.

On Thursday morning, four Palestinians were buried at Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis after being killed in an Israeli drone strike in the al-Mawasi area of Rafah, near the Rafah and Karem Abu Salem (Kerem Shalom) crossings.

Abu Amra said the victims were civilian employees of the Ministry of Economy who monitor aid trucks entering through Karem Abu Salem.

More than 30 others were wounded in the attack, according to Al Jazeera’s Moath al-Kahlout. Tens of thousands of displaced Palestinians live in tents in al-Mawasi, which Israel had previously designated a “safe zone”.

Al-Kahlout also reported that 11 people, including women and children, were wounded when Israeli artillery struck a house east of Gaza City, citing emergency services.

Gaza’s Health Ministry said on Thursday that six Palestinians had been killed and 38 wounded over the previous 24 hours.

The violence came as the ministry renewed its call for the Rafah crossing to be opened so that sick and wounded Palestinians can leave the territory for treatment.

In a statement, the ministry said 21,468 patients and wounded people need to travel for care outside Gaza, including 6,430 identified as priority cases.

It blamed repeated border closures and what it described as deliberate delays in evacuation procedures for worsening patients’ conditions, saying dozens had died while waiting for permission to leave and the health of thousands more had seriously deteriorated.

Since February, 3,056 patients and wounded people have been evacuated for treatment abroad, the ministry said, 2,614 through Rafah, which connects Gaza with Egypt, and 442 through the Karem Abu Salem crossing with Israel.

articles.title: Merthyr man saved by off-duty police sergeant after cardiac arrest
articles.summary: James Ashley from Merthyr Tydfil suffered a cardiac arrest in a shop in Cwmbran.
articles.body:
A dad who suffered a cardiac arrest and collapsed in a shop said his 12-year-old son could have lost his dad if a "hero" off-duty police officer had not saved him.

James Ashley, 52, from Merthyr Tydfil, had just finished parkrun and was shopping in Cwmbran when he was hit by a "wave of dizziness" and fell to the floor on 4 April.

Sgt Adam Hollings from Gwent Police was nearby and immediately started CPR.

"I clinically died twice but by the time the paramedics got there, I was sitting up talking... the difference with Adam knowing what he was doing is that my son didn't lose his dad as a 12-year-old," he said, and called him an "absolute hero".

Hollings, who has spent 21 years on the force, was awarded a Royal Humane Society Resuscitation Certificate for his role in saving Ashley's life.

"We're very lucky to have the first aid training that we do, and if we can occasionally be in the right place at the right time to help people out, then fantastic," he said.

The 40-year-old from Abergavenny told Radio Wales Breakfast that even though he was off-duty his training and lifesaving skills kicked in and he acted on "autopilot".

He told someone in the shop to call an ambulance, and then used a defibrillator.

A defibrillator is a device that gives a jolt of energy to the heart . It helps get the heart beating again when someone is in cardiac arrest and their heart has stopped.

Ashley was taken to University Hospital Wales in Cardiff and has since made a full recovery.

"The difference with Adam knowing what he was doing is that my son didn't lose his dad as a 12-year-old," he said, calling his saviour an "absolute hero, a legend".

The pair were reunited a week later when Hollings visited in hospital.

"The nicest moment in all of it was meeting James and his family," Hollings said.

"Being able to see that me doing a little bit there got him to the hospital in time so he could have the lifesaving care that he needed, and know that he was there for his family, that's the real reward.

Ashley said Hollings was a "lifesaver", but also "just a smashing bloke".

Ashley had undergone first aid training himself from a previous job and said even though he was "rusty now", he encouraged others to use their skills if they have them or to get the training.

"If you think, 'Oh, you know, I'm sure there'll be someone there' and 'Oh, it's someone else's opportunity to do it' or 'I can't be bothered or whatever', you absolutely can make a difference to people's lives," he said.

"And it's not just maybe the person you save, it's the people around them who you're helping."

Sharon Owen, CEO of Calon Hearts, a Welsh charity that provides defibrillators and training, praised Hollings for his "quick thinking".

She said it showed "just how important it is to know CPR and have the confidence to act."

"When someone suffers a cardiac arrest, every second counts," Owen added.

"Don't be afraid of getting it wrong - call 999, start CPR and follow the call handler's instructions.

"Doing something is always better than doing nothing."

Owen said people needed to try to overcome any embarrassment they have about performing CPR on a stranger.

"Research shows that women are less likely than men to receive CPR, partly because people may feel uncomfortable touching a woman's chest.

"But when someone's life is at risk, embarrassment should not come into it. Everyone deserves the same chance of survival."

If you find someone collapsed, make sure it's safe to approach

Check if they respond by gently shaking their shoulders and asking them loudly "are you ok?"

If they don't respond, shout for help and ask someone to call 999 or 112 for an ambulance, or put your phone on hands-free and call yourself

Open their airway by gently tilting their head back and lifting their chin, and look, listen and feel for up to 10 seconds for normal breathing

Kneel by the casualty and put the heel of your hand on the middle of their chest. Correct hand placement for CPR on a person with breasts may mean that your hands may touch some of the breast. This is okay

Put your other hand on top of your first hand and if you can, interlock your fingers

Lean forwards so your shoulders are over your hands, keep your arms straight and press down hard to a depth of about 5-6cm before releasing the pressure, allowing the chest to come back up. Push at a rate of 100 to 120 per minute

Listen to instructions from the 999 operator if you still have them on the phone. They will tell you what to do and help you to push at the right speed

Continue chest compressions until emergency help arrives or the person starts showing signs of life and starts to breathe normally

articles.title: Many with ACA coverage face a new crisis in 2027: Insurers fleeing the market
articles.summary: Courtney Mroch was already paying a high price for health insurance when she learned her insurer, Cigna, was pulling out of Tennessee’s Affordable Care Act marketplace.
articles.body: Courtney Mroch was already paying a high price for health insurance when she learned her insurer, Cigna, was pulling out of Tennessee’s Affordable Care Act marketplace. The 56-year-old Nashville resident has diabetes and asthma and is a cancer survivor. She pays $1,250 a month for a silver plan this year, up from $850 a month in 2025 — more than her family’s mortgage. To keep costs down, her husband is enrolled in a separate, non-ACA plan that’s less expensive. “Who knows who will cover me in 2027 or how much more it’ll cost,” Mroch said. Many Americans are heading into ACA open enrollment with the likelihood of higher premiums and fewer insurance companies to choose from. In most states, the enrollment period begins Sunday, giving people who buy their own coverage about two months to compare plans for next year. Insurers who offer ACA plans are proposing a premium increase of about 15%, on average, for 2027 — the second straight year of double-digit increases, according to an analysis from KFF, a nonpartisan health policy research group, that looked at public filings from insurers across all 50 states and Washington, D.C. At the same time, 11 insurers have announced plans to leave the ACA marketplaces in 2027 in at least some states where they currently offer coverage, according to KFF. Among them is Cigna, which will exit all 11 states where it offers ACA plans and has more than 350,000 ACA enrollees. Six insurers have announced plans to enter new marketplaces. “The main takeaway is that more insurance companies are leaving the marketplace than coming in,” said Cynthia Cox, director of the program on the ACA at KFF. For people shopping for coverage, that could mean fewer insurers to choose from and more people having to switch plans. “This is going to create a lot of discontinuities in care and coverage for people,” said Miranda Yaver, an assistant professor of health policy and management at the University of Pittsburgh. “If you have a doctor who doesn’t accept the fewer number of options that are available to you, that can be very disruptive, especially if you’re someone who has a chronic illness.” “And if the fewer available price points don’t work for you, are you going to remain covered?” she added. Why are insurers leaving? The departures come after the enhanced tax credits expired at the end of 2025, leading ACA enrollment to fall by roughly 3 million. Some healthier people moved to cheaper but worse coverage or dropped insurance altogether. Those who remained on their plans tended to have greater health needs and higher medical costs. Overall, that can make the marketplace less profitable for insurers as healthcare costs rise, said Jennifer Chumbley Hogue, an insurance broker in Texas. From the consumer perspective, that means “constant upheaval, whether it’s the plan pulling out or the subsidies have changed or the doctor network has changed,” Hogue said. In an email, a Cigna spokesperson pointed to April comments from CEO Brian Evanko, who said that leaving the ACA marketplace aligns with goals to position the company’s “core healthcare businesses for sustainable growth.” For some families, rising premiums alone had already forced difficult financial decisions. Denise O’Connor and her husband saw their monthly premiums in Colorado more than double this year, from just over $900 to about $2,300, forcing them to dip into their retirement savings. The O’Connors are also covered by Cigna. She plans to work with a broker to find another plan, but her husband is also considering going uninsured for about six weeks until he qualifies for Medicare. “It’s a worry,” she said. “He’s healthy, but anything can happen at any time.” Mark Lathrop, who lives in Idaho and owns a winery just across the state line in Washington, said he and his wife are also looking for new coverage after their insurer, PacificSource, decided to leave the ACA marketplace. The couple is already facing higher costs. They don’t qualify for the standard ACA subsidies, and Lathrop said a comparable plan for 2027 would cost about $17,600, up from about $16,000 last year. He needs an annual MRI to monitor a spinal cord injury, which costs $2,400, making a plan with a lower deductible important. “We don’t know what we are going to do yet,” he said. In a statement, a PacificSource spokesperson said the decision to exit the ACA marketplace was not “made lightly” and was made to ensure it can “continue fulfilling our mission and serving members for the long term amid growing pressures across the healthcare industry.” Yaver said the changes could undermine public support for the ACA. As fewer people enroll and those who remain face higher costs and fewer options, the marketplace could become less attractive to consumers — weakening the law without the Trump administration and Republicans ever having to repeal it. A recent KFF poll found overall public favorability toward the ACA dropped to 58% from 64%. “We don’t see the repeal and replace of 2017, but we’re making it much harder for patients to remain on these plans,” Yaver said. Hogue urged enrollees to review their options when open enrollment begins, rather than rely solely on the notices they receive in the mail. The premium and subsidies available to them, she said, may be different from the amounts listed in those letters. “It’s worth the five minutes to take a look,” she said.

articles.title: 6 People Have Died From Flu in Connecticut in the Past Month as Cases Rise Nationwide
articles.summary: The flu has hit the U.S. earlier than usual this year. And the virus has already caused six deaths in Connecticut, the state’s department of public health says.
articles.body: The state of Connecticut has already recorded its first flu-related deaths in a flu season that’s hit earlier than is typical. Six people have died since the week ending in Sept. 26, according to new data from the Connecticut Department of Public Health. That week saw the first death, followed by three more in the week ending in October 17 and another two deaths in the week ending in October 24. All six Connecticut residents who’ve died from influenza so far this season were age 55 or older, the department says. There have also been nine COVID deaths since September in the state. “Our hearts are with the families and loved ones of the people that have been lost. These deaths are a sobering reminder that flu can be serious, especially for older adults, and that respiratory virus season is already here,” Dr. Manisha Juthani, commissioner of the Department of Public Health, said in a press release. This time last year, Connecticut had not recorded any flu-related deaths, data show. Flu cases in the state have increased more than 22% since last week and flu-related hospitalizations have increased more than 64%. That increase is similar to what public health experts are seeing in much of the country as the flu arrives earlier in the season than usual this year. An Early Flu Season While no two flu seasons are identical, cases typically pick up around October and last through March, the Mayo Clinic says — though it’s not unusual for cases to linger through May. It’s still too early to know exactly how the 2026-2027 flu season will play out, but experts told TODAY.com they’ve noticed a concerning trend: Flu cases began to tick up as early as August this year. While cases are still low overall, they are growing in much of the U.S., according to data from the Center for Disease Control and Prevention. The most recent CDC data available indicate a nearly 6% increase in positive flu tests in the last week. An early flu season does not necessarily mean a severe flu season, however, the experts said. A newly mutated version of the H1N1 influenza A strain is thought to be responsible for many of the current early flu cases, TODAY.com reported previously, but it’s too early to know whether this version of the virus leads to more serious illness. How to Stay Safe To protect yourself and your family from the flu, you can get a flu vaccine. Experts typically recommend getting your flu vaccine before the end of October. And this year’s vaccine is already available at pharmacies, clinics and doctors’ offices. “If you haven’t gotten it yet for whatever reason, now’s the time to get vaccinated because the flu season is starting a little bit sooner and you need at least two weeks for the vaccine immunity to (reach) protective levels,” Andrew Pekosz, Ph.D., a virologist at the Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health, told TODAY.com previously. Vaccination is especially important for those considered to be at a higher risk for severe flu complications, which includes older adults, young children and those who are immunocompromised. Getting your vaccine now will also ensure that you’re at a solid level of immunity heading into the winter holiday season. In addition to getting vaccinated, you can also: Wear a well-fitting mask or N95 respirator in crowded indoor settings.Wash your hands frequently.Get tested or test yourself if you develop flu symptoms. And keep in mind that flu isn’t the only illness circulating right now. Both COVID and RSV are also in the mix, and it’s worth making sure you know how to protect yourself from those viruses as well.

articles.title: Targeted drug shrinks tumors in 3 out of 4 patients with advanced breast cancer
articles.summary: A phase 3 clinical trial published in JAMA found trastuzumab rezetecan linked to 73% lower risk of cancer progression or death versus chemotherapy.
articles.body: There may be a promising new treatment on the horizon for advanced breast cancer patients, according to developing research. Researchers are studying the cancer-killing drug trastuzumab rezetecan for those with ERBB2-low metastatic breast cancer, whose tumors have low levels of HER2, a protein that can help cancer cells grow. A phase 3 clinical trial called HORIZON-Breast06 sought to determine whether the drug works better than standard chemotherapy for patients with this cancer type. SHIFT IN CANCER SCREENING GUIDANCE HAS EXPERTS CLASHING OVER NEW GUIDANCE The researchers analyzed 551 female patients across 73 hospitals in China who were randomly assigned to receive either the drug intravenously every three weeks, or the physician’s choice of chemotherapy. The study period lasted from June 2023 to August 2025. The drug significantly delayed cancer progression compared with chemotherapy, giving patients more than a year before their cancer began growing again. The median time without tumor growth was 16.4 months compared to 6.8 months with chemo. FDA APPROVES ONCE-DAILY PILL FOR DEADLY CANCER AFTER PATIENTS' SURVIVAL RATES NEARLY DOUBLE Patients who received trastuzumab rezetecan were 73% less likely to have their cancer worsen or die during the study than patients who received chemotherapy. The drug appeared to delay cancer progression in patients with both hormone receptor-positive and hormone receptor-negative breast cancer. The results were published in JAMA. Tumors shrank in 75.5% of patients who received the drug, compared with 41.2% of those who received chemotherapy. At the 12-month mark, 90.6% of trastuzumab rezetecan patients were alive, compared to 81.4% of chemo patients. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER The authors concluded that trastuzumab rezetecan provided "significant progression-free survival benefit over physician’s choice of chemotherapy in patients with ERBB2-low advanced breast cancer." Loren Rourke, a Texas-based breast surgical oncologist and author in Texas, called the results "incredibly encouraging." "When you're talking about women living with advanced breast cancer, those months matter," Rourke, who was not involved in the study, told Fox News Digital. "They represent more time when the cancer is being held in check and potentially more opportunities to enjoy life without the disease getting worse." What makes these findings especially exciting, according to the oncologist, is that the treatment showed benefits across different types of breast cancer. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES "It's another important step forward, and it gives us genuine reason to be hopeful," she said. "A treatment that can keep cancer from progressing for a longer period has the potential to make an enormous difference in a patient's life." While the drug may cause fewer serious lung problems than similar treatments, it was linked to other side effects, including anemia and other blood-related problems. "It's another important step forward, and it gives us genuine reason to be hopeful." Serious side effects occurred in more than 84% of patients who received the new drug, compared with nearly 68% of those who received chemotherapy. Rourke emphasized the importance of considering the side effects, "because more time without cancer progression doesn't automatically mean better quality of life." "We need to better understand the side effects, particularly the significant decreases in blood counts that can lead to fatigue, anemia and increased risk of infection," she said. The researchers acknowledged that toxicity occurred more frequently and often required dose modification, although they said these effects were "generally manageable." TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ The experts agreed that more research is needed. "As exciting as these findings are, there are still important questions we need to answer," Rourke told Fox News Digital. "We know this treatment delayed cancer progression, but we don't yet know whether it will help patients live longer. That's an important distinction." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "It's important to celebrate meaningful progress while making sure we're asking the right questions about what comes next."

articles.title: Judge blocks ‘medically frail’ definition in Medicaid work requirement rule
articles.summary: A federal judge on Thursday blocked President Donald Trump's administration from enforcing a rule that would narrow exceptions to new work requirements for Medicaid recipients with serious medical conditions.
articles.body: A federal judge on Thursday blocked President Donald Trump's administration from enforcing a rule that would narrow exceptions to new work requirements for Medicaid recipients with serious medical conditions. U.S. District Judge Richard Stearns in Boston sided with 25 states and the District of Columbia, which had argued that the new rule would force medically frail people to clear unnecessary hurdles to maintain government-funded health insurance coverage. The Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services, the agency that adopted the rule, did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Medicaid, the government health insurance program for low-income Americans, is jointly funded by the federal and state governments. CMS issued the rule in June in order to implement work requirements for Medicaid that were enacted as part of Trump's signature tax and spending measure, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which he signed into law last year. The law requires adults aged 19-64, with a few exceptions, to complete a minimum of 80 hours of work or community engagement activities per month or be enrolled in an education program at least half time to qualify for Medicaid beginning January 1, 2027. CMS’s rule provided guidance to states on how to implement the work requirements, including the law’s exemptions for individuals who are “medically frail or otherwise have special medical needs.” But Stearns said CMS’s rule unlawfully limited who qualifies as “medically frail” by dictating that the exemption only applies if someone’s “physical, mental, or other behavioral health condition significantly impairs the individual’s ability to comply with the community engagement requirement.” “Because enforcement of an unlawful definition of ‘medically frail’ may lead to the disenrollment of otherwise eligible vulnerable individuals relying on Medicaid coverage for continuity of care, the States (and public) face potential for great hardship in the absence of an injunction,” Stearns wrote. The judge was appointed by former President Bill Clinton, a Democrat. While he invalidated that part of the rule, he upheld other provisions that Democratic-led states had also challenged. Among those states were California, Massachusetts and New Jersey, whose attorneys general led the legal challenge.

articles.title: Drake, Ann Michael Maye donate $25k in sports gear to Chelsea students
articles.summary: Patriots quarterback Drake Maye and his wife Ann Michael Maye recently gifted more than $25,000 in sports gear to students of Chelsea High School.
articles.body:
A group of Massachusetts student-athletes just received a surprise from two New England celebrities .

On Wednesday, Oct. 28, New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye and his wife Ann Michael Maye gifted more than $25,000 in sports equipment to students at Chelsea High School. The school's football team and coaches received helmets, shoulder pads, footballs and other gear from Drake Maye himself.

The donation, made through a partnership between the MayeDay Family Foundation and Boston-based nonprofit Good Sports , "marks the launch of Power Up Play, a partnership focused on supporting after-school sports programs at high schools across New England," according to a press release.

"Beyond providing essential equipment, the partnership aims to give young athletes the confidence, resilience and life skills they need to succeed in the classroom, in their communities and in life," the release continues.

Photos: Drake, Ann Michael Maye donate sports gear at Chelsea High School

Launched in March 2026, the MayeDay Family Foundation is a nonprofit founded by Drake and Ann Michael Maye with the goal of providing assistance and support to children and families enduring hardship so that they may achieve a brighter future, according to the foundation's website . The Mayes' foundation will support various programs throughout New England, such as Boston Children's Hospital, as well as in their home state of North Carolina.

Back in May 2026, the charity hosted its first activation, a celebrity softball match at Polar Park in Worcester, Massachusetts. The inaugural game raised over $500,000.

In September 2026, the Mayes donated $15,000 from the foundation to fulfill the Amazon wish lists of all teachers and support specialists at Providence's Alfred Lima Sr. Elementary School.
authors: Catherine Messier, USA TODAY NETWORK - New England

articles.title: What Is Volume Eating? Dietitian Shares Her No. 1 Strategy for Feeling Full on Fewer Calories
articles.summary: Volume eating can be a useful tool if you’re looking manage your weight, but there are a few things to keep in mind if it’s a practice you’d like to follow.
articles.body: Typical weight loss advice calls for portion control and restriction. But one eating pattern lets you put more food on your plate without sending your calorie count soaring: high-volume eating. “The idea is to focus on foods that provide a lot of volume for relatively few calories, such as vegetables, fruit and broth-based soups,” registered dietitian Erin Palinski-Wade tells TODAY.com. “These foods tend to be naturally rich in water and fiber, which can help you feel satisfied with fewer calories overall.” While this might sound like a plus — a calorie deficit without the mind-consuming hunger — there are some factors you’ll want to keep in mind, says Palinski-Wade. What Is Volume Eating for Weight Loss? “I like to think of it as a strategy for building more satisfying meals rather than another restrictive diet,” says Palinski-Wade. It’s especially helpful if you’re trying to lose or maintain a certain weight but struggle to feel full and satisfied, she adds. Rather than slashing your portions sizes or completely cutting out higher calorie foods you love, you can change some of the foods you eat so that you can eat larger, more filling portions of them for fewer calories. This way, you leave your meals feeling satiated and, in some cases, you might find you have leftover or unused calories in the “bank” for the occasional higher-calorie food or treat. The research shows this can work, too. One analysis that looked at 31 studies found that reducing the calorie or energy density in one’s meals helped to reduce overall caloric intake. “Other research has found that people eating lower energy-density diets could actually consume 1-2 pounds more food per day while taking in fewer calories and losing more weight over six months,” adds Palinski-Wade. Who Should Consider Volume Eating? People looking to manage their weight, whether losing it or maintaining it, might find volume eating to be a useful tool. It can feel discouraging to reduce the amount of food on your plate when you’re used to a certain amount and miss that feeling of comfortable fullness at the end of your meals. “Choosing more high-volume foods may make it easier to manage calories without feeling deprived,” says Palinksi-Wade. Even if weight management isn’t your goal, there are still benefits to volume eating. Palinksi-Wade says those of us who eat out of habit, boredom or tend to emotionally eat can turn to this practice for the familiar and soothing sensation of chewing and eating. “And for the many Americans who aren’t eating enough fruits and vegetables,” she adds, “focusing on adding more volume through produce can be a great way to improve overall nutrition.” Who Should Avoid Volume Eating? While volume eating is useful for some, Palinski-Wade urges caution for a few different groups To start, for someone with a current or past eating disorder, including binge eating disorder, “this approach may reinforce an unhealthy relationship with food or feelings of fullness,” she says. If you notice your focus shifts from seeking a feeling of satisfaction after a meal to consuming the largest amount of food for the fewest possible calories while ignoring your body’s hunger and fullness cues, volume eating isn’t for you. “People with certain digestive conditions, such as IBS, Crohn’s disease or other forms of inflammatory bowel disease, may also struggle with large amounts of high-fiber foods,” says Palinski-Wade. “Anyone with a history of bowel obstruction, bowel surgery, or difficulty absorbing nutrients should speak with their healthcare provider before significantly increasing fiber intake.” Anyone on a GLP-1 will also want to be cautious. Eating large portions, even if they’re low in calories, can worsen nausea and gut discomfort since these medications slow digestion. “For these individuals, prioritizing protein and nutrient-dense foods in smaller portions is generally a better strategy,” says Palinski-Wade. Finally, anyone who burns calories at a fast rate should avoid volume eating. Think athletes, or highly active gym-goers, runners or swimmers, will find it hard to consume enough energy from high amounts of low-calorie foods to support their movement, performance and recovery. How to Practice Volume Eating Prioritize Foods High in Water and Fiber Think foods like leafy greens, cucumbers, peppers, berries and watermelon, says Palinkski-Wade. These foods take up a lot of space on your plate (and in your stomach) without adding significantly to your overall daily caloric intake. When It Doubt, Try Soup One strategy, she suggests, is to start your meals with a broth-based soup to make your meals more satisfying for fewer calories. “One study found that people who ate two servings of low-calorie-density soup each day lost 50% more weight over a year than those consuming the same calories from snack foods,” says Palinski-Wade. “And including a wider variety of low-energy-density foods may also help improve overall diet quality.” Keep in Mind When Volume Eating… Volume eating can impact your hunger and fullness cues in ways that are both beneficial and detrimental. On the upside, you’ll experience the familiar sensation of comfortable fullness from lower-calorie foods as they take up space in your stomach. “That physical stretching sends signals to your brain that you’re getting full, which may help you feel satisfied while consuming fewer calories,” Palinski-Wade says. However, volume alone shouldn’t be your priority. It might cause you to lose sight of balanced meals. Your focus for every meal should be consuming adequate amounts of protein, carbs, healthy fats, fiber, vitamins and minerals. Eating all the essential macro and micronutrients are just as important for satiety. “The goal should be to feel comfortably satisfied after eating, not to feel as physically full as possible,” says Palinksi-Wade. While you’re eating, check in with yourself. Halfway through your meal, pause and ask yourself whether you’re still hungry or eating because the food is in front of you. “It can take about 20 minutes for your brain to fully register feelings of fullness,” she says. “Slowing down and checking in with yourself during a meal can make a big difference.” If 20 minutes after your meal you find you’re still hungry, go ahead and eat more.
